reviews.review: This 3rd Person shooter is set in the Warhammer world and is worth buying.
Fun game, simple action. Clearly more story for those into the Warhammer Lore, but it was entertaining. I found the final battle difficulty to be quite difficult to defeat on the hardest difficulty.

This was actually the first game I got on Steam, back when people still used Cds to activate them through the cd-key here. (WAIT FOR A DISCOUNT, this game is old and DOESN'T DESERVE SUCH A HIGH PRICE!)

Nonetheless, the ugly parts first. This is a short game with an unfulfilling last boss battle and some lackluster twists. Some of the guns don't progress well in the main campaign (the storm bolter should have replaced the main bolter instead of being a side-arm, ending a lackluster and late add to a roster of far better weapons), and the multiplayer is rather dead. No one will try the extra maps and extra modes (most folks just go for point battles in casual maps), the only thing to progress through the quirks and perks of the online weapons is through pvp, which will be riddled with cheaters or a severe lag made worse by the fact that the hosts keep changing. The DLC is just aesthetic, so unless you are a hardcore fan wanting to sport your favorite chapter's armor in battle, don't even think of buying those.

[h1]Why the thumbs up?[/h1] 

So far, this is [b]THE[/b] best Warhammer game to date to express not only the scenario itself, with gargantuan machines and buildings, the callous nature of the universe and how brutal it can be with humankind (even if Orks are mean to be a parody of hooligans), but the role of the space marines. From how they act, the dynamics of the scenario (one space marine versus a legion, how they treat/are treated by the other factions, how strong they are), but also the minutiae such as how a bolter 'feels' and sounds, plasma rounds and so on. The game offers you a power trip of how mighty a space marine feels with a throng of ork goons to be minced, but isn't shy of humbling you with specialized troops that can fold your 'invulnerability' like paper tissue [spoiler]and making things far worse with Chaos Space Marines in the second half giving you a taste of your own medicine[/spoiler]. Most weapons are true to the scenario, giving you a varied set of options on how to deal with special situations, and it will offer you specific weaponry at the right times ('sniper' weapons in 'sniping sections' and so on).

Also, this game was a giant middle finger to Games Workshop handling of the franchise (alongside the lore) and gaming industry practices at the time. When everyone wanted bombastic triple-A games, the dev teams wanted nothing more than a fun ride through the Grim Darkness of the 40th millenium. They sought to be loyal to the source material, but weren't shy on delivering some punches, such as, hiring Mark Strong (might is he!) to voice Captain Titus, one of the best examples of what a Space Marine should be. This was during the Matt Ward era of Warhammer, where the Ultramarines were elevated to the status of nearly psychopathic Mary-Sues that that were praised by everyone, and to see Titus, a Captain of the Ultramarines, to be a humble person, interested more in the safekeeping of a planet and its populace instead of glory and most of all, willing to adapt to the situation instead of following the Codex blindly (ironically, lore-wise, CLOSER to what the founder of the Ultramarines wanted), was a gut-punch for many and a pleasant surprise by most.

So if you are interested in a gory glorious gargantuan quest that won't take much of your mind plot-wise but awe you with designs and characterization, get it!
Recommended for those interested in 40K settings. Great architecture, classic and effective gameplay.
